name: Bog
notes: Ombrotrophic raised/blanket bog: rain-fed acid peat, Sphagnum carpets, cottongrass, heath dwarf shrubs, carnivorous sundews, stunted bog pines. Drawn on Scandinavia/British Isles/Baltic and Canadian muskeg.

canopy.name: Bog pine
canopy.source: Pinus sylvestris, stunted bog form on Eurasian raised bogs 1-8 m, sparse crown; Pinus mugo subsp. rotundata on Alpine bogs

canopy.name: Black spruce
canopy.source: Picea mariana, dominant stunted tree of N American bog/muskeg 2-10 m, narrow spire

canopy.name: Tamarack
canopy.source: Larix laricina, Canada/NE USA bogs and fens, deciduous conifer 3-15 m turning gold

shrub.name: Heather
shrub.source: Calluna vulgaris, dominant on British/Scandinavian blanket bog hummocks, evergreen 20-60 cm, purple flowers

shrub.name: Bog rosemary
shrub.source: Andromeda polifolia, circumboreal bogs, low evergreen shrub 10-40 cm with pink bell flowers

shrub.name: Bog myrtle
shrub.source: Myrica gale, N Europe and N America bog margins and wet heath, aromatic deciduous shrub 0.5-2 m

shrub.name: Leatherleaf
shrub.source: Chamaedaphne calyculata, dominant shrub of N American bog mats, circumboreal, evergreen 0.3-1.2 m

shrub.name: Cranberry
shrub.source: Vaccinium oxycoccos, circumboreal Sphagnum bogs, creeping vine on moss carpets with red berries

ground.name: Sphagnum moss
ground.source: Sphagnum magellanicum, circumboreal and S American raised bogs, red hummock-forming peat moss

ground.name: Cottongrass
ground.source: Eriophorum vaginatum (hare's-tail cottongrass), circumboreal bog tussock former, single white cotton head 20-60 cm

ground.name: Round-leaved sundew
ground.source: Drosera rotundifolia, circumboreal Sphagnum bogs, carnivorous red rosette 2-6 cm

ground.name: Deergrass
ground.source: Trichophorum cespitosum, blanket bogs of British Isles/Scandinavia/N America, wiry tussock 10-40 cm

ground.name: Pitcher plant
ground.source: Sarracenia purpurea, N American bogs Canada to Florida, purple-veined pitcher rosette 10-30 cm

special.note: Catalogue plants (data/plants) whose band centres fall inside this biome's climate; computed, informational. Phase 6 may raise their density here so they are findable.

associations.name: Sphagnum-cottongrass raised bog
associations.where: open bog center and hummock-hollow plain, rain-fed acid peat

associations.name: Heather-deergrass blanket bog
associations.where: gently sloping uplands with high rainfall, shallow peat over rock
associations.source: Scirpus cespitosus-Eriophorum blanket mire (Rodwell 1991 M17; Lindsay 1995)

associations.name: Black spruce-leatherleaf muskeg
associations.where: forested bog margin and slow-drained flats, deep peat, cold

associations.name: Bog pine hummock wood
associations.where: drier raised hummocks and bog rim on deep peat
associations.source: Pino mugo-Sphagnetum and Vaccinio uliginosi-Pinetum bog woodland (Ellenberg 1988; EU habitat 91D0)
